pr_title: Fix score no longer being saved when quick-restarting after pass
pr_body:
- Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/30642

The `PerformExit` path ensures the score is imported even if the user restarts after passing the beatmap during the one second completion delay `RESULTS_DISPLAY_DELAY`. 

In https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/30623, `Restart` no longer calls `PerformExit`, therefore discarding the score for the scenario in question.

I've resolved the issue by still calling `PerformExit` rather than letting the `PlayerLoader` do the exiting process.

I wanted to write a test case for this but timing is critical, I'll have to change the constant to be overridable and make my test case set the delay to infinity, but it feels weird to break parts of the component itself in order to test it. I can still write a test case if wanted.

issue_context.title: Replay is not saved when quick retrying at the end of a beatmap
issue_context.body:
### Type

Game behaviour

### Bug description

When pressing "quick retry" after the final note of the beatmap (and before the scorecard appears), a replay is not saved locally even though the score has been submitted.

### Screenshots or videos


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad429e5b-b441-40c8-9a92-c5fcfa89efc3

![osu_lazer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aab264d8-8462-4dc3-b2d7-76305b9f1603)


### Version

2024.1115.1-lazer

### Logs

[compressed-logs.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17774368/compressed-logs.zip)
comments: I would... not have suspected any of the retry changes to break this as they only touched `PlayerLoader`. This needs to be investigated all the same though.
This actually regressed with https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/30623, as it made the quick restart path no longer call `PerformExit` in `Restart`, which prevented the score from being imported.

review_comments: What's with the rename? I preferred the old name.

I'd say it's because the `PlayerLoader` is no longer responsible for performing the restart, ie. calling `this.MakeCurrent()`. the `Requested` terminology implies that another component is going to make the decision of whether a restart should actually occur.
I have ignored adding back the `!ValidForResume` assertion as I think it's a given since the screen is not current and the current screen is presumed to be the results screen.
